title: Swaps reported as expired while they could still land
body:
Until about 17:49 UTC on 11 September, every swap the API built carried a lastValidBlockHeight about 5.5 seconds out. Fogo keeps a blockhash valid for roughly 3000 blocks, about two minutes; the engine had taken Solana's 150-block lifetime, first as a constant and then from its RPC provider, which reports the same Solana figure for Fogo. The chain disagrees: swaps signed 20 and 60 seconds after they were built both landed.

Clients that stop waiting at lastValidBlockHeight, including this site's swap panel and the SDK's browser example, told anyone who took more than a few seconds to approve in their wallet that the swap had expired, while it could still land. Retrying from that message could produce a second swap. We do not know how many users hit it. If you saw "Transaction expired before it landed", check your wallet history before swapping again.

The engine now measures the lifetime on Fogo's own node at startup and reports the chain's figure: about two minutes.

title: /instructions returned every lookup table, making client-built swaps take about a minute
body: Until about 17:23 UTC on 11 September, POST /api/v1/instructions returned all 250 registered address lookup tables for any swap, including one that touches a single pool. A client has to fetch the tables before it can build the transaction, which took 55 to 65 seconds per swap in our tests, against about 1.5 seconds for POST /swap. Amounts were never affected. It now returns only the tables that actually shrink the transaction, usually one or two, and client-built swaps finish in about 2.5 seconds.

title: ExactOut swaps delivered the requested amount minus our fee
body:
Until about 17:11 UTC on 11 September, an ExactOut swap delivered the amount you asked for minus Vulcx's 15 bps fee, and minus the integrator's fee when one was set: a request for 10000 units landed 9985. The on-chain program takes the fee out of the output, and the engine sized the route for the requested amount itself. The fee was the published rate; it came out of the output instead of the input, so an exact-output swap was not exact. We have not established when this began. ExactIn swaps were not affected.

The engine now routes for the requested amount plus the fees, so you receive exactly what you asked for and the fee comes out of the input. amountOut in responses is now that gross figure, consistent with every other response: you receive amountOut minus platformFeeAmount minus integratorFeeAmount.

title: Routing unavailable for 27 hours after an upstream RPC outage
body:
Between 07:07 UTC+1 on 1 September and 10:16 UTC+1 on 2 September, GET /api/v1/quote returned "no route found" for every pair. Quotes, swap building and the WebSocket stream were all affected. No funds were at risk at any point — Vulcx never holds them, and a swap that cannot be quoted cannot be built or signed.

The trigger was upstream: the RPC provider the engine reads pool state from lost its feed and answered every request with "node is unhealthy: no feed from upstream". Fogo's public node was returning 502 over the same period, so this was chain-wide infrastructure rather than one provider.

Three faults of our own turned that into a full outage instead of a degradation. The engine loads its pool set once at startup and, on failure, logged an error and gave up rather than retrying — so a routine restart during the upstream outage left it holding no pools, permanently. /health answered 200 the entire time, because it checked only that the process was alive, not that it could route. And the deploy script, which waits for that 200, fell out of its wait loop on timeout and reported success anyway. Every layer that should have surfaced this stayed quiet.

All three are fixed. Pool loading now retries with backoff until it succeeds; /health is a readiness check that returns 503 with the pool counts while the graph is empty; and the deploy script fails loudly instead of reporting success. The recovery was the new behaviour working: when the upstream feed returned, the engine reloaded 343 pools on its own on retry attempt 171, with nobody touching it.

What we are still missing is monitoring that alerts on this without a person looking. The status page you are reading only checks when someone opens it.
